summary: Morrow County, OR lookout site: 60' wooden L-4 built in the 1930s, staffed 1934-1937, now gone; the Forest Service lists the site as an open scenic stop.

facts.status_note: Gone per the Former Fire Lookout Sites register and firelookout.com; the Forest Lookouts history lists it as removed, undated

access.note: Forest Service lists the Potamus Point Interpretive Site as open with a scenic view; a tourism listing calls it a stop on the Blue Mountain Scenic Byway

visit.trail_note: Forest Service page says potable water is not available at the site; no source describes the tower remains

events.note: Planned three-mile telephone line to the emergency lookout station on Potamus; the tower itself was built in the 1930s (no exact year given)
Max Buschke listed as lookout personnel
Owen Leathers listed as lookout personnel
Forest Service triangulation disk stamped POTAMUS 1936 set under the center of the tower (described in a later survey note)
Jim Stevens reported back at the lookout in an August 19, 1937 notice; an August 26, 1937 notice says he had not returned
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on June 25, 2011

notes_for_editor: No source gives a removal date. The Forest Service interpretive page does not mention the lookout, so nothing describes the tower footprint today. Access is taken from the Forest Service listing and a tourism page. Staffing names come from firelookout.com and 1937 newspaper notices quoted by Forest Lookouts. Brief record matched on height (60 ft) and elevation.
